original_brief.default:
Create an original wooden pavilion using real 3D cellular-automata aggregation. Make this a connected Relay workflow starting from this template: Perplexity research → Codex writes the reproducible CA/Blender script → Blender runs the simulation, builds the pavilion and renders a growth animation → Gemini visualizes the actual completed pavilion → a brief editable PowerPoint explains the process.

Use one coherent equal-length timber system for supports and canopy, with emergent sculptural geometry and a walkable opening. Use deterministic seeded local neighbourhood rules; disclose imposed envelope and passage constraints. Show actual recorded growth generations as cells, then the same occupied graph as timber. The growth animation must be produced by the Blender workflow, not an independently staged browser animation. Keep the camera at pedestrian eye height (1.6 m), far enough outside to frame the whole pavilion. For Gemini, use the actual Blender view to make a realistic landscaped-park photograph with a few people, preserving the design and eye-height camera. No external reference image or named architect.

The growth animation can be used in a 9:16 reel alongside the workflow and final deliverables. Use a configured Codex connection for model nodes and a connected Perplexity browser. Preserve previous jobs. Keep existing limits. Ask before any paid Gemini call or exact native-script execution that requires approval. Do not execute during composition. Do not fake missing animation support or completed results; identify any unsupported connection.
